slides.title: Trig Functions of Any Angle
text: General Definition: For any angle θ with point P(x, y) on its terminal side at distance r from the origin:
r = √(x² + y²) is always positive — signs depend on x and y

slides.title: Reference Angles
text: Reference Angle (θ'): The acute angle (0° to 90°) formed between the terminal side and the x-axis. Always measured to the nearest part of the x-axis.

slides.title: Reference Angles — All Four Quadrants
text: The reference angle is always the same "core" acute angle — it tells you which special triangle values to use.

slides.title: Reference Angles in Degrees — Type 2
text: Strategy: First find a coterminal angle between 0° and 360°, then apply the reference angle formula.

slides.title: Reference Angles in Radians
text: Test Prep: Problem 2b asks for the reference angle of θ = 9π/7. Since 9π/7 > π (Q III): θ' = 9π/7 − π = 9π/7 − 7π/7 = 2π/7

slides.title: Signs of Trig Functions — ASTC
text: Why? sin = y/r, cos = x/r. The sign depends on whether x and y are positive or negative in that quadrant.

slides.title: Determining Quadrant from Trig Signs
text: Strategy: List which quadrants satisfy each condition, then find the intersection.
Given: tan θ > 0 and cos θ < 0
tan > 0 in Q I, Q III
cos < 0 in Q II, Q III
Given: sin θ > 0 and sec θ < 0
sin > 0 in Q I, Q II
sec < 0 → cos < 0 in Q II, Q III

slides.title: Finding Trig Values from a Point
text: Terminal side of θ passes through (−3, 4). Find all six trig values.
csc θ = 5/4 sec θ = −5/3 cot θ = −3/4
Point is in Q II → sin positive, cos & tan negative ✓

slides.title: Test Prep — Trig Values from P(−2, −5)
text: Test 3, Problem 4b: Find the exact trig values of θ with terminal side through P(−2, −5).
x = −2, y = −5 → Point is in Q III
Q III check: sin −, cos −, tan + ✓

slides.title: Finding Other Trig Values from One
text: Given tan θ = −3/4 and sin θ < 0, find sin θ and cos θ.
tan < 0 → Q II or Q IV; sin < 0 → Q III or Q IV
tan θ = y/x = −3/4 with Q IV signs → x = 4, y = −3

slides.title: Evaluating with Reference Angles
text: Find the exact value of: sin 240° and cos 315°

slides.title: Test Prep — Angles from Trig Values
text: Test 3, Problem 3: Find two angles between 0° and 360° where sin θ = √3/2.
sin > 0 in Q I and Q II

slides.title: Area of a Triangle Using Trigonometry
text: Area = ½ · b · c · sin A
Two sides and their included angle
Area = ½ · a · b · sin C
Area = ½ · a · c · sin B
Works for any triangle (not just right triangles) when you know two sides and the included angle. This formula is on the Test 3 reference sheet.

slides.title: Test Prep — Triangle Area
text: Test 3, Problem 7: Find the area of a triangle (not a right triangle). A = 76°, b = 34, c = 21.
Area = ½ · b · c · sin A

slides.title: Test Prep — Coterminal & Reference Angles
text: Test 3, Problem 2: Sketch, find positive & negative coterminal angles, and the reference angle.
Sketch: 97° clockwise → terminal side in Q III

slides.title: Module 11 Summary
text: Always acute (0°–90°), always measured to the x-axis. Find coterminal first if needed.
All Students Take Calculus — determines which trig functions are positive in each quadrant.
sin θ = y/r, cos θ = x/r, tan θ = y/x. Use point (x, y) on terminal side with r = √(x² + y²).
